props.gloss_en: the Sages sought to suppress the book of Ecclesiastes because its words contradict one another
and why did they not suppress it? because its beginning is words of Torah and its end is words of Torah
its beginning is words of Torah, as it is written: 'what profit has man of all his labour which he labours under the sun' (Eccl 1:3)
the school of R' Yannai: under the sun he has none; before the sun, he has
its end is words of Torah, as it is written: 'the end of the matter, all having been heard: fear God and keep His commandments, for this is the whole man' (Eccl 12:13)
R' Elazar: the whole world was created only for the sake of this one
R' Abba bar Kahana: this one is weighed against the whole world
Shimon ben Azzai (or Shimon ben Zoma): the whole world was created only to accompany this one
the verse: 'vexation is better than laughter' (Eccl 7:3)
the verse: 'of laughter I said: it is praiseworthy' (Eccl 2:2)
the verse: 'and I praised joy' (Eccl 8:15)
the verse: 'and of joy: what does it accomplish?' (Eccl 2:2)
'vexation is better than laughter': better the anger the Holy One shows the righteous in this world than the laughter the Holy One laughs over the wicked in this world
'of laughter I said: it is praiseworthy' -- this is the laughter the Holy One laughs with the righteous in the world to come
'and I praised joy' -- the joy of a mitzva
'and of joy: what does it accomplish?' -- this is joy that is not of a mitzva
to teach you that the Shekhina rests neither out of sadness, nor laziness, nor laughter, nor frivolity, nor chatter, nor idle words, but only out of a matter of the joy of a mitzva
as it is said: 'and now bring me a minstrel; and when the minstrel played, the hand of the Lord came upon him' (II Kings 3:15)
Rav Yehuda: and so for a matter of halakha
Rava: and so for a good dream
any Torah scholar who sits before his teacher and whose lips do not drip bitterness -- [his lips] shall be burnt
as it is said: 'his lips are lilies, dripping flowing myrrh' (Song 5:13)
do not read 'flowing myrrh' (mor over) but 'flowing bitterness' (mar over)
do not read 'lilies' (shoshanim) but 'that study' (sheshonim)
no difficulty: this [joy] is of the teacher, that [bitterness] of the student
or say: both are of the teacher -- this before he opens [the lesson], that after he has opened
as Rabba: before he opened for the Rabbis he would say something humorous and the Rabbis were cheered; at the end he sat in awe and opened the lesson
and the book of Proverbs too they sought to suppress, for its words contradicted one another
why did they not suppress it? they said: the book of Ecclesiastes -- did we not analyse it and find a reason? here too let us analyse
the verse: 'do not answer a fool according to his folly' (Prov 26:4)
the verse: 'answer a fool according to his folly' (Prov 26:5)
no difficulty: this one [answer a fool] is in words of Torah (mapping fixed by 30b.9; see header)
that one [do not answer a fool] is in worldly matters (mapping fixed by 30b.8-9; see header)
a man came before Rebbi and said: your wife is my wife and your sons are my sons. He said to him: would you like to drink a cup of wine? He drank and burst
a man came before R' Chiyya and said: your mother is my wife and you are my son. He said to him: would you like to drink a cup of wine? He drank and burst
R' Chiyya: Rebbi's prayer availed him, that [the man] not make his sons mamzerim
for Rebbi, when he prayed, said: may it be Your will, Lord our God, that You save me today from the brazen and from brazenness
the verse the student cites: 'there is nothing new under the sun' (Eccl 1:9)
Rabban Gamliel: in the future a woman will give birth every day
as it is said: 'the woman with child and she who gives birth together' (Jer 31:7)
Rabban Gamliel: come and I will show you its like in this world -- he went out and showed him a hen
Rabban Gamliel: in the future trees will yield fruit every day
as it is said: 'and it shall bear branches and make fruit' (Ezek 17:23) -- as a branch [grows] every day, so fruit every day
Rabban Gamliel: come and I will show you its like in this world -- he went out and showed him a caper bush
Rabban Gamliel: in the future the Land of Israel will yield cakes and garments of fine wool
as it is said: 'let there be abundant grain in the land' (Ps 72:16)
Rabban Gamliel: come and I will show you its like in this world -- he went out and showed him truffles and mushrooms; and for the fine garments, the fibre sheath of a young palm shoot

objections.gloss_en: ומאי דבריו סותרין? כתיב טוב כעס משחוק, וכתיב לשחוק אמרתי מהולל! -- one verse prefers vexation to laughter, the other praises laughter

answered_by.gloss_en: לא קשיא: better God's anger at the righteous in this world than His laughter over the wicked in this world; the praised laughter is His laughter with the righteous in the world to come (= p_tov_kaas_al_tzaddikim, p_lischok_im_tzaddikim)

objections.gloss_en: כתיב ושבחתי אני את השמחה, וכתיב ולשמחה מה זה עושה! -- one verse praises joy, the other disparages it

answered_by.gloss_en: ושבחתי -- the joy of a mitzva; ולשמחה מה זה עושה -- joy that is not of a mitzva (= p_shibachti_simcha_shel_mitzva, p_lesimcha_sheeina_shel_mitzva)

objections.gloss_en: איני? והאמר רב גידל אמר רב: a scholar before his teacher whose lips do not drip bitterness -- they shall be burnt; so a matter of halakha is not approached in joy

answered_by.gloss_en: לא קשיא: הא ברבה, הא בתלמידא -- joy for the teacher, bitterness for the student (= p_ha_berabba_ha_betalmida)
ואיבעית אימא: both of the teacher -- before he opens, joy; after he has opened, awe (= p_kodem_pticha_leachar_pticha)

objections.gloss_en: ומאי דבריו סותרים? כתיב אל תען כסיל כאולתו, וכתיב ענה כסיל כאולתו

answered_by.gloss_en: לא קשיא: הא בדברי תורה, הא במילי דעלמא (= p_ane_ksil_divrei_torah, p_al_taan_milei_dealma)

objections.gloss_en: ליגלג עליו אותו תלמיד, אמר: אין כל חדש תחת השמש!

answered_by.gloss_en: בא ואראך דוגמתן בעולם הזה -- he showed him a hen (= p_dugma_tarnegolet)
